task.description:
Gate lib/letflow/design/iss0430-notify-listen-decision.md for idiomatic OTP usage, supervision integrity, scope creep, and decision-record consistency -- the last hard gate before this design-only WF-03 run closes. CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (step-02b) and SECURITY-REVIEWER (step-02c) have both independently PASSed; do not simply concur with their verdicts -- your job is a DIFFERENT lens (OTP idiom, decision-record consistency, scope), not a re-run of theirs.

Specifically check: (1) does the proposed Letflow.Notify.Listener placement (a new child of Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure, wrapping a Postgrex.Notifications connection) represent sound OTP supervision design -- a GenServer wrapper around a long-lived external connection, restart semantics inherited from Infrastructure's plain OTP-default intensity -- or does it introduce any anti-pattern (e.g. should reconnect/re-LISTEN logic live inside the GenServer's own handle_info, which the design gestures at but does not implement -- confirm the design correctly scopes this as implementation-time detail rather than glossing over a real supervision concern); (2) does the design's decision to explicitly NOT retrofit either already-shipped poller (Question 6) risk scope creep in the OTHER direction -- i.e. does deferring the retrofit leave anything in an inconsistent or half-done state, or is 'standalone, unconsumed infrastructure' a clean, complete deliverable on its own; (3) is the design consistent with every decision record it touches -- decision 0003 (schema-per-tenant), decision 0009 (test-parallel pool sizing, cited for the new connection's budget impact) -- read both decision records yourself and confirm the design doesn't silently contradict either (per core-directives.md's 'Never resolve a conflict silently' -- if you find any tension, it must be flagged, not quietly worked around); (4) is the design consistent with ISS-0425's now-completed resolution (REQ-219/REQ-220, the supervision-tree layering) -- confirm the design treats that layering as settled ground rather than re-litigating or contradicting any of REQ-219's own decisions (restart-intensity choices, :one_for_one at every level, PollersBreaker's role); (5) any scope creep -- does the artefact stay within ISS-0430's own 8 ACs, or does it wander into deciding things ISS-0430 didn't ask it to decide (e.g. final channel names, exact reconnect backoff -- check that these are correctly left as 'Open Questions' rather than silently decided as if final). This is a hard gate: FAIL with the specific gap if anything above doesn't hold.
acceptance_criteria: OTP supervision-design soundness of the proposed Letflow.Notify.Listener placement assessed on its own idiomatic merits, not merely re-confirming CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's structural check
Confirms Question 6's 'not now' retrofit decision leaves no inconsistent or half-done state
Design's consistency with decision 0003 and decision 0009 independently confirmed by reading both records
Design's consistency with ISS-0425/REQ-219's now-completed supervision-tree layering confirmed, not silently contradicted
No scope creep beyond ISS-0430's 8 ACs -- items correctly left as Open Questions are not silently treated as decided
PASS or FAIL stated explicitly with evidence; on FAIL, next_action names CODE-DESIGNER for rework with the exact gap

result.summary: PASS. Reviewed on the REVIEWER lens (OTP idiom, supervision integrity, decision-record consistency, scope creep), independently of CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's structural/AC check (step-02b) and SECURITY-REVIEWER's INV-1 sign-off (step-02c). (1) SUPERVISION SOUNDNESS: the proposed Letflow.Notify.Listener -- a thin GenServer wrapper owning a Postgrex.Notifications connection internally, placed as a new child of Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure immediately after Letflow.Repo/Ecto.Migrator -- is idiomatic. A GenServer (not gen_statem) is the correct tool: a LISTEN connection has one operational mode (connected+subscribed) with reconnect-as-retry, not a multi-state protocol a state machine would model better; no case-state-do crutch standing in for gen_statem is present or implied. The design correctly identifies that re-subscribing (re-issuing listen/2 after every disconnect/reconnect cycle) must live inside the wrapper's own handle_info, and correctly scopes this as implementation-time detail (deferred per AC8) rather than glossing over it as a non-issue -- it names the concern precisely (a fresh Postgrex.Notifications connection has no LISTEN state after auto-reconnect) without writing the callback. Restart-intensity inheritance (Infrastructure's plain OTP-default 3/5s, deliberately NOT Pollers' loosened 5/60s) is reasoned correctly on its own merits: a connection that cannot stay up to Postgres at all is a severe-fault signal, matching Letflow.Repo's own position in the same supervisor, not a transient per-tick fault Pollers' looser budget exists to tolerate. No anti-pattern found. (2) QUESTION 6 'NOT NOW': the Cross-module dependencies section explicitly states no dependency from either poller to Letflow.Notify.Listener, called out as 'a deliberate absence, not an oversight.' The listener is a genuinely complete, standalone deliverable -- it starts, connects, issues listen/2 for known channels, and requires no consumer to be functioning infrastructure. Invariant I2 is correctly phrased as a forward-looking constraint on a FUTURE consumer, not an assumption one exists now. No half-done state found. (3) DECISION-RECORD CONSISTENCY, independently read: decision 0003 -- the design's Question 2 answer (push all tenant-isolation enforcement onto the existing :prefix-scoped fetch, invent no NOTIFY-layer isolation) is a direct, correct application of Dimension B (schema-per-tenant via :prefix, no session/connection-level tenant context, addendum explicitly rejects a GUC mechanism) -- no contradiction. decision 0009 -- the design correctly identifies the new Postgrex.Notifications connection sits outside Repo.pool_size but occupies a Postgres max_connections slot, ties this correctly to 0009's addendum TEST_NONPOOL_CONNECTION_RESERVE concept (citing the existing tenant-schema-reaper connection as the real precedent), and explicitly flags -- rather than silently assumes covered -- that the new connection must be added to that reserve (Open Question 2). No silent contradiction of either record; the one open budget item is flagged, not glossed over. (4) ISS-0425/REQ-219 CONSISTENCY: the design treats Infrastructure/Pollers/PollersBreaker/Http as settled ground. It keeps :one_for_one at every level, respects Pollers' restart:temporary/PollersBreaker-as-sole-restarter arrangement (ISS-0451) by explicitly reasoning why the listener must NOT go inside Pollers (would wrongly subject it to PollersBreaker's restart logic and risk cascading a LISTEN blip into both pollers restarting), and respects the Infrastructure-to-Pollers supervisor-boundary ordering guarantee (ISS-0429) by placing the new child earlier in Infrastructure's own list, never touching the boundary. No re-litigation of REQ-219's decisions found. (5) SCOPE: Open Questions 1, 3, and 4 (trigger-vs-application-emitted NOTIFY mechanism, exact channel name strings, reconnect/backoff behavior) are correctly left open, not silently decided as final -- matching AC8's no-implementation bar and ISS-0430's own 5 design questions plus the retrofit question, nothing more. No abstractions, behaviours, or generic pub/sub plumbing beyond one wrapper GenServer and one connection appear; the 'real-time push path to web/' is named as explicitly future/out-of-scope, not designed toward. MINOR, non-blocking observations for the record: (a) the design does not state whether Letflow.Notify.Listener would be boot-gated like the pollers (start_scheduler/start_service_task_dispatcher-style config key) once implemented -- correctly out of scope for a design-only artefact under AC8, but whoever implements Question 1 should not start it unconditionally in test without also resolving Open Question 2's TEST_NONPOOL_CONNECTION_RESERVE update, which the design already flags. (b) Question 2's extensive malicious-listener security analysis overlaps ground SECURITY-REVIEWER's own gate covers -- not scope creep against ISS-0430's ACs (AC4 requires the isolation mechanism to be named) and SECURITY-REVIEWER still independently re-derived its own verdict rather than accepting it, so the redundancy discipline held; noted only as a pattern to watch, not a gap.
